title: Optimize `Array.resize` by using `memset` (through new `is_zero_constructible` type trait)
body:
`Array.resize` must initialize new elements to valid values. This is currently implemented with a `for` loop calling the constructor.

Some types (e.g. `Variant`) happen to have a default value as all-0 bytes. This can be exploited by using `memset` over all elements instead of iterating in a loop. `memset` is faster than `for` loops because of hyperoptimized implementations. Right now, compilers (at least `clang`) seem not to realize this to insert `memset` automatically.

I have arbitrarily marked some types that I found to be zero-constructible as such. This should carry over the performance improvement to types like `PackedVector2Array` and `PackedStringArray`.

## Benchmarks

I benchmarked a ~6x performance improvement of `Array.resize` (when resizing to a very large size).

```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	var array := []
	array.resize(500000000)
```

(before)
```
523.12 Mc  100,0 %	              Array::resize(int)
523.12 Mc  100,0 %	               Error CowData<Variant>::resize<true>(long long)
481.84 Mc  92,1 %	                Variant::Variant()
481.84 Mc  92,1 %	                 Variant::Variant()
469.45 Mc  89,7 %	                  Variant::'unnamed0'::()
469.45 Mc  89,7 %	                   Variant::'unnamed0'::()
``` 

(after)
```
89.67 Mc  100,0 %	              Array::resize(int)
89.67 Mc  100,0 %	               Error CowData<Variant>::resize<true>(long long)
89.67 Mc  100,0 %	                void memnew_arr_placement<false, Variant>(Variant*, unsigned long)
89.67 Mc  100,0 %	                 __bzero
```

For some reason, in this particular test the profiler showed no performance loss from the allocation itself. Not sure why that is - perhaps because it's just reordering pages for the new array? It's also possible that it's just profiler accuracy problems.
In any case, the performance improvement will likely be less substantial for smaller arrays.

I also benchmarked `range(500000000)` performance, as a sanity check. The impact of `resize` sank from 520.63 Mc(9,0% of total) to 187.75 Mc (3,3% of total) in this case.

Edit: Looks like the final binary is also 46kb smaller (macOS, `template_debug`, `debug_symbols=yes`).

## Addendum

zero-initializable data could be even further optimized by using `calloc` instead of `malloc` for allocation. The reason is that new pages come pre-cleaned from the OS, which makes `memset` calls unnecessary.
This will notably not work for `realloc` calls, so it would be good to switch to an allocation library soon that offers failable `realloc` functions. Further, I'd like to see at least https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100619 merged before I work on that so all my changes don't diverge too much...
